item.title: PM Marape: ‘JSB meeting reached important step for PNG-Bougainville future today’
item.description: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape says a historic threshold has been reached in relations with Bougainville, following the formal end of joint consultations on the region's 2019 independence referendum. At a meeting of the Joint Supervisory Body [JSB] at Melanesian Haus in Port Moresby, Mr Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama endorsed the Joint Consult
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape says a historic threshold has been reached in relations with Bougainville, following the formal end of joint consultations on the region's 2019 independence referendum.

At a meeting of the Joint Supervisory Body [JSB] at Melanesian Haus in Port Moresby, Mr Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama endorsed the Joint Consultation Report and a new Melanesian Framework.

The agreement clears the way for the referendum results to be formally tabled on the floor of PNG's National Parliament on August 27.

Nearly 98 per cent of Bougainvilleans voted for independence from Papua New Guinea in the non-binding 2019 vote. Under the terms of the 2001 Peace Agreement, PNG's parliament retains the final decision on whether to grant full sovereignty.

Marape said the national government had met all its constitutional obligations and that MPs must now vote on the outcome according to conscience and the national interest.

"While we cannot rewind history, we must construct our future as a people," Marape said.

"The work since 2001 has seen many JSBs, many meetings, many exchanges, that has culminated in the implementation of Section 338 of our National Constitution as far as calling a referendum is concerned."

He emphasised that the upcoming parliamentary vote would not mark an end to ties between PNG and the autonomous region, but represented the next phase in a 25-year peace process.

As part of the resolutions reached at the summit, the JSB agreed to hand over all locally generated revenue including taxes from fisheries, mining, forestry, and land, to the Bougainville government by December 31 this year to build the region's fiscal capacity.

Future political and administrative cooperation between Port Moresby and Buka will be managed under the Melanesian Framework.

Marape paid tribute to the patience of Bougainvilleans and urged calm across both regions as the matter moves into its parliamentary phase.

"The Peace Agreement clearly says parliament will determine the final result," he said.

"Section 342, subsection 2 says parliament will make this decision. Whatever that decision is to the people of Bougainville and Papua New Guinea, we must respect the parliament process.

"And that is not the end... the Speaker of the National Parliament then will pass the result and the decision to the Speaker of the Bougainville Parliament."

The Prime Minister called on citizens to pray for wisdom and unity, adding that PNG had demonstrated to the world how complex national questions could be resolved peacefully through constitutional democracy.

item.title: Gamai calls on LLG leaders to stay in communities as new chamber opens
item.description: The new Fly Gogodala local level government [LLG] chamber was officially opened on Monday at Tapila Station in the Delta Fly district of Western by local MP and Livestock Minister Agena Gamai. The decision to construct the chamber was passed in 2024 by members of the District Development Authority [DDA] board.
item.content:encoded:
The new Fly Gogodala local level government [LLG] chamber was officially opened on Monday at Tapila Station in the Delta Fly district of Western by local MP and Livestock Minister Agena Gamai.

The decision to construct the chamber was passed in 2024 by members of the District Development Authority [DDA] board.

The new facility will house local government operations and administration, bringing decision-making and service delivery closer to the rural population of Fly Gogodala.

Speaking during the opening ceremony, Gamai told the local community that following his election in 2022 as the pioneer Member for Delta Fly, his vision was to ensure that administrative operations were not concentrated solely at the district headquarters.

"My vision was to build the seat of government in all the LLG growth centres," Gamai said.

"Today marks the fulfillment of part of that vision that I had, and others will follow."

Gamai encouraged all LLG presidents to return to their respective areas and remain stationed with their people to ensure basic services reach the grassroots level.

The chamber opening was part of a broader community programme that also featured the official opening of a new Evangelical Church of Papua New Guinea [ECPNG] building to serve the spiritual needs of the Tapila community.

Additionally, a dinghy was presented to the Tapila Health Centre to support emergency transport and movement for health workers and patients in the riverine district.

The ceremony was witnessed by DDA members, LLG presidents for Tabo, Fly Gogodala, and Bamu, former Fly Gogodala leadership, as well as community members from Tapila and surrounding villages.

item.title: 18th Sepik River crocodile & arts festival kicks off
item.description: Festivities of the three-day show that promotes the rich cultural heritage of the Sepik River and draws visitors into East Sepik started today. The 18th Sepik River Crocodile & Arts Festival was officially opened this morning by Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk with a strong emphasis to improve tourism in the Sepik River region.
item.content:encoded:
Festivities of the three-day show that promotes the rich cultural heritage of the Sepik River and draws visitors into East Sepik started today.

The 18th Sepik River Crocodile & Arts Festival was officially opened this morning by Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk with a strong emphasis to improve tourism in the Sepik River region.

"We need to bring back the glory days of Ambunti, Angoram, Gawi, and Ambunti must collaborate and bring tourists back," Wiruk said.

"Tourism of cultural events has contributed to cultural, social, and economic development of the region."

Sharing similar sentiments, Provincial Minister of Culture and Tourism Godfrey Wakraai, revealed plans to revive dying cultures in the province.

Wakraai, the president of Gawanga LLG in Ambunti Drekikir district was among the dignitaries in attendance during the opening ceremony of the festival.

The 18th Sepik River Crocodile & Arts Festival rides under the theme 'Keeping and strengthening tourism through Arts, Culture, and Environment'.

The first day of activities showcased a variety of performances from different cultural groups from both Sepik River communities their neighbors - Wosera and Maprik.

The festival is sponsored by a number of groups including Frieda River Limited [FRL] - a partner that has been committed to supporting the show since 2011.

item.title: Western PHA prepares reporting system for province-wide immunisation campaign
item.description: The Western Provincial Health Authority is rolling out a new digital reporting system ahead of its province-wide Catch-up Routine Immunisation Campaign in August and September, with support from PNGSDP and World Vision PNG. A two-day Training of Trainers workshop concluded yesterday in Daru for South Fly District team leaders to equip them with skills to use the Digital Health Information Software
item.content:encoded:
The Western Provincial Health Authority is rolling out a new digital reporting system ahead of its province-wide Catch-up Routine Immunisation Campaign in August and September, with support from PNGSDP and World Vision PNG.

A two-day Training of Trainers workshop concluded yesterday in Daru for South Fly District team leaders to equip them with skills to use the Digital Health Information Software 2 [DHIS2], and the Kobo Collect tool.

The tools will be used to track progress and conduct surveys to identify factors contributing to low immunisation coverage.

Following the Daru training, team leaders will conduct facility-based training across South Fly District. The same training will be extended to other districts, with North Fly and Middle Fly districts scheduled for August 10th to 11th in Kiunga.

PNGSDP has supported the campaign with 86 Android tablets for 86 teams across the province. The tablets will be given to designated data capturers in each team to ensure data entry does not distract clinicians, who will focus on vaccinating children.

The digital system will help WPHA’s Monitoring and Evaluation teams keep accurate records of children immunised during the campaign.

The initial target group is children under one year of age. However, WPHA chief executive officer Dr. Miriam Boga said the campaign will also include older children following reports of a new measles outbreak in New Ireland Province.

"We have also made an exception to include older children as the country now reports a new measles outbreak in the New Ireland Province," Dr. Boga said.

Executive Manager for North Fly District Health Services Galeva Sere closed the Daru training and acknowledged partners for their technical support in developing the reporting framework WPHA will use.

The Catch-up Routine Immunisation Campaign is scheduled for North Fly and Middle Fly from August 17th-28th, and South Fly and Delta Fly from September 7th-18th.

item.title: JSB endorses consultation report, Bougainville referendum vote heads to National Parliament on August 27
item.description: The Joint Supervisory Body has formally endorsed the Post-Consultation Report and the Melanesian Agreement in Port Moresby today, clearing the path for the Bougainville referendum results to be tabled in the National Parliament on August 27. Co-chaired by Prime Minister James Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama, the special meeting marked the official conclusion
item.content:encoded:
The Joint Supervisory Body has formally endorsed the Post-Consultation Report and the Melanesian Agreement in Port Moresby today, clearing the path for the Bougainville referendum results to be tabled in the National Parliament on August 27.

Co-chaired by Prime Minister James Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama, the special meeting marked the official conclusion of post-referendum negotiations following the historic 2019 vote, where 97.7 per cent of Bougainvilleans voted for independence.

Under the agreed framework, the referendum outcome will be presented to the floor of Parliament for formal debate, with both leaders set to jointly determine the specific date for the decisive vote.

Addressing media following the closed-door session, Prime Minister Marape commended the resilience and patience of the people of Bougainville as both governments navigate the final constitutional stage of the peace process.

"This marks an important journey," Marape said. "The JSB we are having this morning is historic before we bring to rest the 97.7 per cent results of the referendum.

"Peace in 2001 was a construct of leadership from both sides as we tried to rest the civil crisis and move toward a future that is amicable. Section 342 of our Constitution clearly says Parliament will make this decision, and whatever that decision is, we must respect the parliamentary process."

However, President Toroama delivered a direct and uncompromising message to the National Government, rejecting any administrative or legal maneuvers aimed at dismissing the independence vote or reverting Bougainville to an extended autonomy model.

Toroama said the National Government’s potential non-affirming decision position was a dangerous legal fiction, and warned against treating Bougainville’s political future as a corporate performance review or political charity.

"Bougainville is moving away from the autonomy space, and let me make that clear," he said. "The question has been asked, answered, and sealed in ink and blood. We do not need a pathway to revisit that question.

"Any attempt by the National Parliament to vote down the referendum result, freeze us in a dead autonomy framework, or demand constitutional amendments is a rejection of the peace process itself."

The ABG President also voiced strong opposition to the unilateral introduction of a three-quarters voting threshold in the National Parliament, stating that the rule was established without the mandatory joint consultations required under the Melanesian Agreement.

Despite these, both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to the overarching spirit of the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement, emphasizing that the ongoing diplomatic oversight of the United Nations remains vital to ensuring international credibility as the transition reaches its climax.

item.title: New police fleet to strengthen operations across Northern Command
item.description: Police in Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands are set to benefit from a new fleet of vehicles under the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary's fleet replacement program. The initiative is aimed at improving police mobility, reducing reliance on hired vehicles and strengthening frontline policing across the Northern Command.
item.content:encoded:
Police in Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands are set to benefit from a new fleet of vehicles under the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary's fleet replacement program.

The initiative is aimed at improving police mobility, reducing reliance on hired vehicles and strengthening frontline policing across the Northern Command.

Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police for Logistics, Chief Superintendent Christopher Smith, said the Constabulary is replacing ageing vehicles with government-owned fleet to improve operational capacity nationwide.

He said the Northern Command, which covers Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands, has experienced transport challenges that have affected police operations and emergency response.

Smith said reducing the use of hired vehicles would allow funds to be redirected towards other policing priorities, including operational resources and service delivery.

The new vehicles would provide officers with reliable transport to carry out patrols, respond to emergencies and deliver policing services more effectively.

Smith said the fleet replacement program forms part of broader efforts under the Special Police Assistance Program [SPAP], which is supporting improvements to police infrastructure, equipment and logistics across the country.

He said the program is designed to ensure police commands have the resources needed to perform their duties efficiently and better serve communities.

Smith also stressed the importance of proper vehicle maintenance and accountability as the Constabulary continues to expand its fleet.

The new vehicles are expected to improve response times and strengthen law and order operations across Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands, while supporting police officers serving communities throughout the Northern Command.

item.title: El Niño and strong winds damage food gardens, disrupt water supply in Markham
item.description: Residents of Ragiampun village in Morobe's Markham district are facing growing hardship as El Niño conditions and strong winds continue to damage food gardens and reduce water supplies. This has been a concern for both the community and nearby schools.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Ragiampun village in Morobe's Markham district are facing growing hardship as El Niño conditions and strong winds continue to damage food gardens and reduce water supplies.

This has been a concern for both the community and nearby schools.

Strong winds have destroyed large numbers of banana trees and damaged other food crops, including taro and sweet potato, leaving many families worried about their food security and income.

The affected gardens are the main source of food and cash income for many households in the community.

Locals said the damage has come at a time when families are relying heavily on their gardens to feed their households, but prolonged dry weather and strong winds have continued to destroy crops.

The dry conditions have also reduced the community's water supply, with creeks and other water sources running low.

The water shortage is affecting both Ragiampun SDA Primary and Adventist High School, where students and teachers are struggling to access enough water for drinking, cooking, washing and other daily needs.

Ward Councillor Kelvin Sauri said the destruction of food gardens and the shortage of water were placing significant pressure on the community.

"The strong winds have destroyed our banana crops, and our water sources are drying up," he said.

"Both of our schools urgently need water. If the water supply is not restored soon, the schools could be forced to close because water is essential for students and teachers."

Community members are calling on local leaders and the Markham district administration to urgently address water supply and assist families whose food gardens have been damaged.

They said the situation indicates the need for more reliable and resilient water infrastructure to support rural communities during El Niño and other extreme weather events.

item.title: RPNGC begins 2027 election prep
item.description: The Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] has commenced early preparations for the 2027 National General Elections, focusing on resource allocation, manpower, and logistical requirements nationwide. Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police [Logistics] Christopher Smith said Police headquarters is working closely with provincial police commands to identify operational needs, including vehicles
item.content:encoded:
The Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] has commenced early preparations for the 2027 National General Elections, focusing on resource allocation, manpower, and logistical requirements nationwide.

Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police [Logistics] Christopher Smith said Police headquarters is working closely with provincial police commands to identify operational needs, including vehicles, equipment, and personnel deployments.

Smith said early planning will allow the constabulary to better prepare for the massive nationwide operation and ensure officers on the ground are adequately supported.

“Logistics will play a critical role in election security, with reliable transport, communications equipment, and other operational resources needed to support police deployments throughout the country,” Smith said.

He said key lessons learned from previous national elections are shaping strategy for 2027, with an emphasis on coordination and operational readiness.

Smith said continued backing from the National Government and key development partners will be crucial to securing the necessary resources to maintain law and order throughout the election period.

Planning will continue over the coming months as provincial commands submit their requirements to headquarters.

item.title: Power restoration underway at Magarima Station
item.description: Electricity is set to be restored at Magarima Station in the Magarima District of Hela Province, with major work now underway to install two new 500 kilowatt generators.

item.title: Western targets 35pc child vaccination rate
item.description: The Western Provincial Health Authority [WPHA] will roll out a province-wide catch-up immunisation campaign next month to address low vaccination rates among infants.
